digest.component_or_area: source code comment taxonomy and relocation (src/rebar)
propositions: Six subsystems identified ~2,033 recoverable comment lines across 439 files by reclassifying prose as history (tickets), architecture (ADRs), contracts (schema), or non-proximate context (delete)
The largest category is self-referential prose explaining the 800-line module cap, occupying the budget it describes; 28 reconciler sites carry variants of this pattern
Three load-bearing files (event_append.py, _processors.py, signing.py) recover minimal lines because their comments document replay-compatibility and security invariants that cannot be relocated

Verified-stale comments were found (six sites claiming P1-P9 while DET_CHECKS runs P1-P11; stale Anthropic constraints in llm/; imports cited as 'later sub-tasks' that already exist) and corrected in-place where they document live invariants
Eight sites repeat the same four-paragraph architecture argument about idempotent transform order; this argument is consolidated into a new ADR and inline blocks collapsed to one-line citations

All dispositions (RELOCATE, DELETE, KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE, CORRECT-IN-PLACE) are assigned to every in-scope comment block; the actual measured net recovery across six shards is 85 lines, far below the ~2,033 pre-triage estimate because moves were relocation-dominated rather than deletion-dominated
